command.tickpilot.explain.no_session: Where the time goes: not measured. Category and per-type costs need a profiling session - run /tickpilot profile %s while the server is loaded
command.tickpilot.explain.session: Where the time goes, over %s profiled ticks at %s ms/tick:
command.tickpilot.explain.main_cost: Main cost: %s, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick)
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.tick_rate: Recommendation: none from these numbers. The tick rate is set by /tick, so TPS and MSPT describe a configured rate rather than server load. Run /tick unfreeze and /tick rate 20, then ask again.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.warming_up: Recommendation: wait for the warm-up to finish and run this again. The first ticks after a start cost far more than a running server does, and they still dominate the averages.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.inconsiste: Recommendation: do not act on the category numbers above. A profiler self-check counter is non-zero, which means one of the hooks is wrong and the breakdown may be misattributed. Please report it with the counters shown.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.profile_fi: Recommendation: run /tickpilot profile %s while the server is under this load. The tick is over budget, but nothing has been profiled, so there is no honest way to say what is spending the time.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.spikes_now: Recommendation: the average is inside budget at %s ms, but p99 is %s ms, so the cost sits in occasional slow ticks rather than in every tick. Run /tickpilot profile %s now, while it is happening - only a session running through one can attribute it.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.past_spike: Recommendation: nothing to change right now. The server is inside its budget at the moment; the p99 of %s ms comes from earlier in the retained history. Run /tickpilot profile %s while it is happening again, not now.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.healthy: Recommendation: no action. Average MSPT is %s against a target of %s, no category is over budget and no drops are in progress.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.entity_typ: Recommendation: reduce how many %s tick. It is the single most expensive type at %s ms/tick over %s instances per tick - remove some, move them apart, or keep fewer of their chunks loaded. TickPilot does not thin them for you: no throttling policy is implemented yet.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.block_enti: Recommendation: reduce how many %s tick. It is the single most expensive type at %s ms/tick over %s instances per tick - remove some, or keep fewer of their chunks loaded. TickPilot does not thin them for you: no throttling policy is implemented yet.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.category_o: Recommendation: the dominant cost is %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick), but this session recorded no per-type costs, so no single culprit can be named. Run another session with per-type accounting enabled before changing anything.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.chunk_ops: Recommendation: the tick is dominated by chunk operations, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick) - loading, generating and unloading chunks, plus mob spawning. Lower view-distance and simulation-distance in server.properties, and pre-generate the area players are exploring. Note that chunk loading for a player is never throttled by TickPilot, so this is not a cost the mod will take away for you.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.scheduled_: Recommendation: scheduled block and fluid ticks dominate, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick). That is usually redstone or flowing liquids. TickPilot cannot attribute this to a block type, so the next step is finding the build - look at what was added recently, especially clocks and large farms.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.random_tic: Recommendation: chunk environment ticking dominates, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick) - random block ticks, weather, ice and snow. Lower simulation-distance, and check whether randomTickSpeed was raised above the default of 3.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.network: Recommendation: connection processing dominates, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick). That is player count, packet volume, or a mod sending a lot of data. TickPilot does not break this down further, so a network-aware profiler is the next step.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.saving: Recommendation: autosave dominates, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick). Check disk speed and how much of the world is changing. A short session that happens to cover one autosave will over-report it - this one was %s ticks, so run a longer one before acting.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.other: Recommendation: the largest share is Other, %s ms/tick (%s%% of the tick) - tick time TickPilot has no injection point for. It cannot be explained from here. A JVM profiler such as Spark or async-profiler is the right tool for this case.
command.tickpilot.explain.rec.unattribut: Recommendation: none can be derived. The profiler produced no category to attribute the tick to.
command.tickpilot.explain.effect.bounded: Expected effect: at most %s ms/tick, %s%% of the measured %s ms tick, and only if every one of them stops ticking. MSPT is already under 50 ms, so this buys headroom against future load, not more TPS. Measure again afterwards - the real effect is not predictable from here.

Expected effect: at most %s ms/tick, %s%% of the measured %s ms tick, and only if every one of them stops ticking. The tick is above 50 ms, so TPS recovers only if it drops back under 50. Measure again afterwards - the real effect is not predictable from here.
command.tickpilot.explain.effect.unknown: Expected effect: unknown. Nothing measured here bounds it, and a number invented now would be worse than this answer. Measure again after the change.
command.tickpilot.explain.effect.measure: Expected effect: none directly - this is a measurement step, not a change.
command.tickpilot.explain.effect.none_ne: Expected effect: nothing to estimate, because no change is being recommended.
command.tickpilot.error: TickPilot hit an internal error; see the server log
